newsitem.title: UK: Dirty tankers mainly flat to softer, quiet.
newsitem.headline: Dirty tankers mainly flat to softer, quiet.

text.p: Dirty tanker rates were mainly flat in quiet Monday trade, but Mideast/Japan very large crude carriers (VLCCs) showed signs of slippage on low enquiry, brokers said.
Mideast/Japan VLCCs eased to W70 from W72.5 last week and from their year high of W75 earlier this month.

A two-tier market in older and newer ships remained in evidence, with the 260,000 tonne, 1977-built Patriotic fixed at W65 to South Korea for Hanwha, while more modern ships achieved at least five points more.
The Mideast/west sector continued moribund, after no fixtures on this route were reported all last week.
The West Africa/U.S. Gulf VLCC market was also quiet, with W67.5/65 still the nominal rate, brokers said.
The 130,000 tonne (Suezmax) sector was steady at W87.5 in the Mediterranean and West Africa/U.S. Gulf.
Brokers said the 80,000 tonne (Aframax) U.K./Cont sector was also a two-tier market, with modern ships from non-Norwegian ports attracting some 10 points more than older vessels.
But one broker said the level of W135 achieved on Friday was "over the top" and W130 was more realistic for a modern ship on Monday, or W115/120 for older tonnage.

Aframaxes in the Med edged up to W125 from W120, with a good supply of cargoes accounting for the firmness. "But I don't think it will go up much more from here. We seem to be at the top of the week, if not the month," an Italian broker said.
European fuel oil was quiet, with 25,000 tonne cargoes in the north easing to W235 from W240 but flat in the Med at about W200.
Caribs/upcoast rates were slightly softer, with 70,000 tonne crude cargoes around W175 and 50,000 tonne fuel oil stems at W192.5, brokers said. --London newsroom +44 171 542 4088
